description: A small, hand-authored retrieval evaluation set. The four source documents in docs/ were written specifically for this evaluation (not copied from any external corpus and not generated by the LLM/retrieval pipeline under test). Chunk boundaries were then produced by actually running the production chunker (services/knowledge/chunking.py::chunk_text) with the real CHUNK_SIZE_CHARS=1000/CHUNK_OVERLAP_CHARS=150 settings, and the relevance judgments below were assigned by reading the real resulting chunk content - they are not the chunks the retrieval system happened to return; they are genuine human relevance judgments made independently of any retrieval run. This is a small illustrative set (4 documents, 5 chunks, 6 queries), not a large-scale IR benchmark - it exists to produce a genuinely measured Recall@K/Precision@K/MRR/nDCG number from a real pipeline execution, not to claim statistical significance at production scale.

queries.query: How does the Calvin cycle fix carbon dioxide?
What happens during the TCP three-way handshake?
How do routers use IP addresses to forward packets?
Why is merge sort considered a stable sorting algorithm?
What is the worst-case time complexity of quicksort and why?
